sources.entry: TableTool - A simple CSV editor for macOS.

summary.one_liner: TableTool is a simple macOS (OS X) editor for CSV files that auto-detects delimiter, encoding and quoting, and lets you edit and convert them in a table view.
summary.what_it_does: The app opens CSV files and automatically detects their format specifications, including record delimiter (comma or semicolon), character encoding, decimal separator and quoting style. It displays the contents in a grid-based table view where cells, rows and columns can be edited. Format specifications can also be set manually when automatic detection is not what you need. It can convert an existing CSV file to a different format. The stated project scope is deliberately limited to being a simple CSV editor, with no formatting options or formulas.
use_cases: Editing CSV files on a Mac
Opening CSV files with semicolon delimiters
Fixing character encoding issues in CSV exports
Creating new CSV files in a grid view
how_to_run: Download TableTool from the Mac App Store (per README)
stack: Objective-C/Swift (not named in README; macOS app)
notable: Automatic detection of CSV delimiter, encoding, decimal separator and quoting style
Grid-based table editing of cells, rows and columns
Converts CSV files to other formats
Deliberately minimal scope: no formulas or formatting features
caveats: Distributed through the Mac App Store per the README
Formatting options and formulas are explicitly out of scope
